He was the top college basketball recruit in 2013.Dodd, Rustin. [http://www.kansascity.com/2013/06/19/4302589/andrew-wiggins-debuts-with-big.html Andrew Wiggins debuts with big dunk in front of KU fans], ''[[Kansas City Star]]'', June 19, 2013. ==Early life== Wiggins was born in [[Toronto]], [[Ontario]]{{cite web|author=Blair, Jeff |url=http://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/blair-time-for-raptors-to-go-all-in-for-wiggins/article12896649/ |title=Blair: Time for Raptors to go all in for Wiggins |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |date=2013-06-28 |accessdate=2014-03-12}}{{cite web|url=http://www.citynews.ca/2013/05/14/toronto-born-basketball-prospect-wiggins-to-play-at-kansas/ |title=Toronto-born basketball prospect Wiggins to play at Kansas |publisher=Citynews.ca |date=2013-05-14 |accessdate=2014-03-12}} and raised in nearby [[Thornhill, Ontario]]. He is the son of former [[NBA]] player [[Mitchell Wiggins]], an American, and former [[Summer Olympic Games|Olympic]] [[track and field]] sprinter [[Marita Payne|Marita Payne-Wiggins]], a Canadian.{{cite web|author=MIKE GANTER |url=http://www.torontosun.com/sports/basketball/2010/12/08/16477156.html |title=Andrew Wiggins: Canada's great basketball hope |publisher=Torontosun.com |date=2010-12-08 |accessdate=2012-09-21}} ==High school career== [[File:20130403 MCDAAG Andrew Wiggins dunking B (9).jpg|thumb|left|Wiggins [[slam dunk|dunking]] in the [[2013 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]] Wiggins attended [[Vaughan Secondary School]] in [[Vaughan|Vaughan, Ontario]] for two years before transferring to [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]] in 2011. Wiggins had been rated as the top prospect for 2014, but announced in October 2012 that he would officially reclassify into his original high school class of 2013, and was immediately placed ahead of the previous number one prospect, [[Jabari Parker]], by [[ESPN]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/8551419/andrew-wiggins-reclassifies-class-2013-new-no-1-recruit|title=Andrew Wiggins in Class of 2013|first=Dave |last=Telep |publisher=espn.com|date=2012-10-25 |accessdate=2012-10-25}} On February 7, 2013, after an article in ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' criticized Canadian basketball and Wiggins' work ethic, he responded later that day, scoring 57 points in a 111–59 win over [[Marietta College]].{{cite web|url=http://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/eh-game/andrew-wiggins-nearly-outscored-opponent-himself-hours-scathing-074256228.html |title=Hoops phenom Andrew Wiggins scores 57 points hours after scathing Sports Illustrated article |first=Neate |last=Sager |publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |date=2013-02-08 |accessdate=2014-03-12}} Wiggins was named the 2013 [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] on February 25.{{cite web|url=http://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/canadas-wiggins-wins-naismith-award-top-high-school-023952460--nba.html|title=Canada's Wiggins wins Naismith award as top high school basketball player in US|accessdate=2013-02-26|date=2013-02-25|publisher=Yahoo! Sports}} He was named the 2013 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] on March 28 as the nation's top high school player. He was the first Canadian player to be so named.Payne, Terrence. [http://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/07/16/kansas-forward-andrew-wiggins-first-canadian-to-win-gatorade-athlete-of-the-year/ Kansas forward Andrew Wiggins first Canadian to win Gatorade Athlete of the Year], ''[[NBC Sports]]'', July 16, 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2013/03/andrew-wiggins-alonzo-mourning-speak-about-gatorade-poy-award/|title=Andrew Wiggins, Alonzo Mourning Speak About Gatorade POY Award|accessdate=2013-03-28|date=2013-03-28|work=[[SLAM Magazine]]|author=Schwadron, Abe}} In May 2013, he was named [[Mr. Basketball USA]].{{cite web|url=http://highschoolhardwood.com/2013/05/08/andrew-wiggins-named-mr-basketball-usa/|title=Andrew Wiggins Named Mr. Basketball USA|accessdate=2013-06-30|date=2013-05-08|work=HighSchoolHardwood.com|author=Flores, Ronnie }} He was ranked number one high school basketball player by ''[[SLAM Magazine]]''.[http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2013/05/slam-fresh-75-2013/ SLAM ONLINE | » SLAM Fresh 75 – 2013] In April 2013, Wiggins played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] All-American game in [[Brooklyn]].[http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5204&path=mbball Andrew Wiggins - 2013-14 Men's Basketball], KU Athletics Department.Berman, Carl. [http://www.huffingtonpost.com/carl-berman/2013-jordan-brand-classic_b_3084178.html 2013 Jordan Brand Classic], ''[[Huffington Post]]'', April 17, 2013. He scored 19 points and tied [[Julius Randle]] for lead scorer for the East team. ==College career== Wiggins committed to the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball]] team on May 14, 2013.[http://www2.kusports.com/news/2013/may/14/top-prospect-andrew-wiggins-chooses-kansas/ Top prospect Andrew Wiggins chooses Kansas], ''[[Lawrence Journal-World]]'', May 14, 2013. Before the announcement, he had narrowed his choices to [[Florida State University]], the [[University of Kentucky]], the [[University of Kansas]] and the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill|University of North Carolina]].Meek, Austin. [http://cjonline.com/sports/2013-05-18/wild-chase-leads-wiggins-ku Wild chase leads Wiggins to KU], ''[[Topeka Capital-Journal]]'', May 18, 2013. Retrieved 2013-05-22. Wiggins joined the Kansas team on June 19, 2013. On January 13, 2014, Wiggins scored 17 points and collected 19 rebounds in a 77–70 victory over [[2013–14 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]], becoming only the second freshman in the last 15 years (along with [[Michael Kidd-Gilchrist]]) to amass those numbers in a win against a ranked opponent.{{cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24408767/wiggins-embiid-impress-make-huge-kansas-statement-in-win-at-iowa-state |title=Embiid, Wiggins wow, make big statement in win at Iowa State |first=Matt |last=Norlander |publisher=CBS Sports |date=2014-01-14 |accessdate=2014-03-12}} Wiggins averaged 17.1 [[points per game]] (ppg), 5.9 [[rebounds per game]] (rpg), and made 34.1% of his three-pointers in his freshman year at Kansas.{{cite web |url=http://www.kuathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=5204 |title=University of Kansas Men's Basketball: #22 Andrew Wiggins |author= |date= |website=KUAthletics.com |publisher=Kansas University Athletics Department |accessdate=19 February 2014}}{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/_/id/67429/andrew-wiggins |title=Player Profile: Andrew Wiggins |author= |date= |website=ESPN.com |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=19 February 2014}} On January 22, 2014, Wiggins was named a Top 25 Finalist for the [[John R. Wooden Award|John R. Wooden Men's Player of the Year]] award by the [[Los Angeles Athletic Club]].[http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=1581 John R. Wooden Midseason Top 25+ Advanced Stats], [[Los Angeles Athletic Club]], January 22, 2014.[http://www.kuathletics.com/news/2014/1/22/MBB_0122141747.aspx Kansas’ Andrew Wiggins Named to John R. Wooden Award Midseason Top 25], KU Athletics, January 22, 2014. On February 28, he was named one of the 10 semi-finalists for [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].{{cite web|title=Top 10 National Semifinalists Named for 2014 Men's Naismith Trophy presented by AT&T |url=http://naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/12/2014-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-presented-by-AT-T-Top-10-National-Semifinalists.aspx|work=Naismith Awards|accessdate=February 18, 2014|date=February 28, 2014}} On March 8, 2014, Wiggins scored 41 points against [[2013–14 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]], the most for a [[Big 12 Conference]] freshman since [[Michael Beasley]] scored 44 points against [[2007–08 Baylor Bears men's basketball team|Baylor]] in 2008.[http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=400498422 West Virginia overcomes Andrew Wiggins' 41 points to stun Kansas] ==Professional career== Wiggins declared for the [[2014 NBA draft]] on March 31, 2014.{{cite web|url=http://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/03/31/kansas-star-andrew-wiggins-to-declare-for-nba-draft/7110755/ |title= Kansas star Andrew Wiggins declares for NBA draft |author=Eric Prisbell and Scott Gleeson |date=March 31, 2014 |publisher=[[USA Today]] |accessdate= 31 March 2014}} ==International== Wiggins participated in the [[2010 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] and 2012 [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]], assisting the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]]'s win of a bronze medal in each tournament.{{cite web|url=http://northpolehoops.com/2012/06/21/canada-captures-bronze-medal-at-fiba-americas-u18-championship/ |title=Canada Captures Bronze Medal at FIBA Americas U18 Championship! |publisher=NorthPoleHoops.com |date=2012-06-21 |accessdate=2013-05-22}} During the 2010 victory, Wiggins was a teammate of [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]], the number one overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite web|url=http://www.basketball.ca/andrew-wiggins-p149064 |title=Andrew Wiggins |publisher=[[Canada Basketball]] |accessdate=2013-07-05}} In the 2012 tournament, he led the team in scoring with 15.2 ppg, along with 7.6 rpg.{{cite web|url=http://turkey2010.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/84794/sid/7548/tid/257/_/2012_FIBA_Americas_U18_Championship_for_Men/index.html |title=2012 FIBA Americas U18 Championship For Men
